items.title: William Russell Interview, 1962-09-04
items.q: it's possible, it might have been that Natty Dominic thing, though, too, or something, he had a tone similar to muted style at times.

ctx.x: I have a note here. He mentioned that there were

three great clarinetists in New Orleans. Piku, Lorenzo Tio, and George Bakke. He didn't think Big Eye Louie was really in the first class. Other people will tell you they think Big Eye was better than Piku and so on. So some of that could be a question of opinion. he thought Dodds wasn't really a first class clarinetist. He was all right. He was only on a couple of his records, maybe four sides or so. I don't know. I even asked him once, I said, is it true that Muggsy had recorded with him? And he said, yes. No,…
He was dead in that two summer.

items.title: William Russell Interview, 1962-08-31
items.q: And also Natty Dominick, who maybe wasn't one of the two or three greatest all-time trumpet players, but certainly had a wonderful rhythmic driving style. One of the choice men as far as personally a wonderful fellow.

ctx.x: He was my favorite of all of them on my own record.

And then also, not that I was just trying to pick Jelly's favorite musicians, but Roy Palmer, whom Jelly also considered the best trombonist. Who had only recorded one very early date with Jelly on an old autograph session. But I had a good interview with him. And also Natty Dominick, who maybe wasn't one of the two or three greatest all-time trumpet players, but certainly had a wonderful rhythmic driving style. One of the choice men as far as personally a wonderful fellow.
Are you going to talk about your personal contact with Jelly?

So, um, I did, uh, record that Roy Palmer I got on trombone and later Kid Ory on trombone. And, uh, um, St. Cyr, of course, and Pops Foster, several bass players. Uh, uh, Ed Garland, Montuti, they call it. He was one of my very favorite musicians. He still plays in California. Well, anyway, I have about 20 interviews, uh, different instruments. Natty Dominic, um, on trumpet. Bunk would have been a logical one. He was already dead. I never did get Louie. I would have tried to get him sometime, although it's a…
And this is on the New Orleans Ensemble Stock.
